known_cutoff_publicity_caveats: Z.ai does not publish a training-data cutoff for GLM 5.3; the structured cutoff remains unknown. Checked 2026-08-30 against the Hugging Face model card (https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3), the vendor guide (https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.3) and the DeepInfra model record. None states one. The release date is not a cutoff and is not used as a proxy for one. Note that GLM 5.3 shares GLM 5.2's base model -- the card states 'GLM-5.3 uses the same base model as GLM-5.2 -- every gain comes from post-training' -- so its pretraining data is at least as old as GLM 5.2's, which is unpublished as well.

GLM 5.3 was announced 2026-08-14, after the Cycle 1 corpus decision window closed and after the corpus anchor of 2026-06-30. This entry is supplementary: it must never be substituted into the frozen Cycle 1 registry, and its rows publish as supplementary_post_anchor rather than official. The classification does not turn on which release date is chosen: the open weights landed roughly two weeks later, on 2026-08-28, and both dates are after the anchor.

NOT GLM-5.3-Flash. That is a different model -- a 320B-A18B natively multimodal MoE released 2026-08-26 at roughly a tenth of this model's price (https://docs.z.ai/guides/vlm/glm-5.3-flash, checked 2026-08-30). This entry is the 743B GLM 5.3 text model at DeepInfra id 'zai-org/GLM-5.3'. The two are one character apart in prose and an order of magnitude apart in price, so any later edit must re-read the model_id rather than the display name.

Execution settings mirror the frozen official successor registry wherever the provider allows it: controlled_docket_tool_only, max_output_tokens 128000, an explicit reasoning setting, and provider-default sampling. Z.ai documents 'a 1M-token context window and a maximum output length of 128K tokens' (https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5.3, checked 2026-08-30), so the official 128000 parity cap is exactly the vendor ceiling and no provider-imposed deviation was required.

reasoning_effort 'high' matches the official successor registry's OpenAI reasoning_effort 'high'. GLM 5.3 accepts only 'low', 'high' and 'max' and defaults to 'max' -- source https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3 model card, checked 2026-08-30: 'GLM-5.3 supports controlling the thinking budget through the reasoning_effort parameter, which accepts three levels: low, high, and max. It defaults to max if not passed (or if set to any other value).' That accepted set is identical to Kimi K3's, which is why GLM 5.3 rides the existing DeepInfra reasoning-effort allowlist unchanged and needs no new reasoning parameter style. Selecting 'high' deliberately overrides the model's own 'max' default DOWNWARD so the setting matches what the official four ran at, exactly as for Kimi K3; the card's advice to 'keep the default max' for leaderboard reproduction is deliberately not followed, because parity with the official four is the controlling constraint here and running GLM at 'max' would give it a reasoning budget the official models did not have. The value is always sent explicitly, never left to the provider default -- and note the card's warning that any unrecognized value silently falls back to 'max' rather than erroring, so a typo would be invisible in the response.

The GLM 5.2 reasoning shape does NOT apply to 5.3. GLM 5.2 nested a separate thinking:{type} toggle alongside a seven-value effort control; GLM 5.3 exposes a flat top-level reasoning_effort with three values, the same spelling the adapter already sends for Kimi K3. Recorded because the adapter's DeepInfra note described the 5.2 shape and was stale for 5.3 as of this entry.

DEVIATION -- served host is not the model vendor, and the served precision is not the vendor's. GLM 5.3 is served through DeepInfra at model id 'zai-org/GLM-5.3', not through Z.ai's own API. DeepInfra reports quantization 'fp4' for this model (https://api.deepinfra.com/models/zai-org/GLM-5.3, fetched directly 2026-08-30), while the released checkpoint on Hugging Face is tagged fp8 and Z.ai publishes no FP4 checkpoint (https://huggingface.co/api/models/zai-org/GLM-5.3, tags include 'fp8', fetched directly 2026-08-30). The served artifact is therefore a host re-quantization of the vendor's weights, not the vendor's weights. This is a stronger caveat than Kimi K3's, whose checkpoint is natively MXFP4 with no host precision choice to make: for GLM 5.3 the host precision IS a choice, and it can change without notice.

DEVIATION -- no request-level version pinning exists. DeepInfra's model id floats to latest, as every host's does for open-weight models. At freeze time https://api.deepinfra.com/models/zai-org/GLM-5.3 returned version '3XP0BkDi', quantization 'fp4' and max_tokens 1048576 (fetched directly 2026-08-30). Preflight must re-read that endpoint before dispatch and REFUSE if version or quantization has changed. Given the fp4 re-quantization above, the quantization field is the load-bearing half of that check for this model. This converts a silent substitution into a loud refusal; it is not, and must never be described as, a request-level pin.

UNVERIFIED PENDING PROBE -- reasoning-token accounting. This is the same open question as Kimi K3's and it is a property of the host, not of the model: as of 2026-08-30 DeepInfra's documentation contains no occurrence of completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens and no response example showing where reasoning tokens are counted. The adapter therefore treats DeepInfra as unverified_conservative and ADDS any reported reasoning tokens, because under-reporting spend against this cycle's provider cap is the unrecoverable direction; response metadata records reasoning_token_accounting=unverified_conservative so a run on this shape cannot be mistaken for a verified one. The one-call shape probe must resolve this before any paid dispatch.

UNVERIFIED PENDING PROBE -- whether 128000 leaves room for the answer. GLM 5.3's reasoning trace is returned separately and shares the completion budget with the answer, and DeepInfra's model record publishes no max_output_tokens of its own (the field is null; only max_tokens 1048576 is given). The adapter reads message.content only and refuses an empty one, so an empty answer is never silently settled -- but a cap that is ample must be confirmed by the probe rather than assumed from the vendor's 128K ceiling.

GLM 5.3's weights are open under a custom non-OSI license named 'glm-5.3' in the model card front matter (license: other, license_name: glm-5.3), not MIT or Apache. DeepInfra rather than this project is the serving operator. Recorded for completeness. Source: https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3, checked 2026-08-30.

No long-context surcharge is published for this model on DeepInfra, so no long_context_surcharge is declared; the flat rate applies across the full context. DeepInfra reports no active discount for it either (pricing.discount is null, fetched 2026-08-30).
pricing_source: https://api.deepinfra.com/models/zai-org/GLM-5.3, fetched directly 2026-08-30: cents_per_input_token 0.00012 and cents_per_output_token 0.0004, i.e. USD 1.20/M input and USD 4.00/M output, with pricing.discount null and cached input at 0.2x the input rate. The same conversion reproduces the already-frozen Kimi K3 prices (2.85/14.25) from the same endpoint, which is how the arithmetic was checked. For comparison, Z.ai's own API lists GLM-5.3 at USD 1.40/M input and USD 4.40/M output (https://docs.z.ai/guides/overview/pricing, checked 2026-08-30); DeepInfra is below the vendor on both sides, which is consistent with it serving a re-quantized fp4 build rather than the vendor's fp8 checkpoint.
release_timestamp_source: Z.ai announced GLM-5.3 on 2026-08-14, initially API- and subscription-only, and stated it would publish open weights about two weeks later once a cyber-capability safety review completed; the Hugging Face repository https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3 reports createdAt 2026-08-25 and lastModified 2026-08-29 (API metadata fetched directly 2026-08-30), consistent with the weights drop landing on or about 2026-08-28. The announcement date is used as the release timestamp, matching how the Grok 4.6 and Kimi K3 entries treat vendor announcements as authoritative. Either date is comfortably after the 2026-06-30 corpus anchor, so the classification is unaffected by the choice. Checked 2026-08-30.
